gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-spline-sans-mono: Spline Sans Mono sets fixed-width, code-style letters in a bold, uniform stroke, with lowercase nearly as tall as the capitals. Tilt Neon then wraps tube-like display letters around it, so the monospace body feels like the quiet engine behind a loud sign.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-tiny5: Tiny5 reads tall and compact, so its ascenders look short and the whole line feels tidy and friendly. Over a longer stretch it stays approachable, and Tilt Neon's tube-like heading never lets the stroke swell or slow the eye.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-truculenta: Tilt Neon hits first with a splayed c and a stroke like bent tubing. Truculenta follows in compact, rounded lines with a tall x-height, and a longer passage would go down smoothly because its forms stay open to the side.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-ubuntu: Ubuntu reads modern and businesslike, its lofty lowercase band filling each line. Ubuntu against Tilt Neon's heading, round letters drawn like bent wire, is the pair's strongest quality: loud wire up top, steady plain sans below.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-victor-mono: Victor Mono is a monospace with loose spacing and bowls left unfinished on one side, so text looks magnified without growing. Tilt Neon handles the shouting with its tubelike, constant-width curves, while Victor Mono does the structured, precise work underneath.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-viga: Viga reads as a plain sans with hairline-free, shadow-free strokes, and its capitals barely stand taller than the letters beside them. Tilt Neon brings the swagger.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-voces: Voces builds its lowercase tall, with stems and hairlines in a close ratio that keeps each line crisp. Tilt Neon's curves are as thick as its straight stems, while Voces thins its joins gently without going spindly.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-winky-rough: Winky Rough sets its lowercase at a height that nearly matches the capitals, giving each line a contemporary, level look. Tilt Neon's line width never swells or tapers, and a longer passage in the plain sans below would feel businesslike.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-winky-sans: Tilt Neon's tube-like stroke never pinches or flares. Winky Sans answers with capitals barely taller than its lowercase, and that quiet, modern evenness against the loud heading is where the pair shines most.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-yantramanav: Yantramanav packs tall lowercase letters close together, nearly reaching the capitals, with spacious gaps at the terminals of its rounded glyphs. Tilt Neon is best at bold, wire-like display strokes, while Yantramanav is best at modern, clean text.
